entries.action: Refine the P1 stacking recipe: meta-learner input = member confidences (probs) + raw features, not hard votes; compare vs majority-vote control. Killer stays MEMBERS-CARRY.
entries.note: stacked generalization done right: the higher-level model must combine lower-level confidences, not just predictions; beats majority vote / arcing / bagging on classification tasks. Our m5g already feeds member outputs (soft) to the ridge — this confirms the recipe and adds the control: any R-BODY stacking run must also report the majority-vote baseline.

entries.title: Issues in Stacked Generalization

entries.action: Design-only R-BODY-3 (behind P1, data/compute-gated): frozen pretrained decoder as member body with only readout trained; killer = P1 stacking-gate vs ridge. Do not reopen M1p2 until a body family passes P1.
entries.note: patched-decoder attention model pretrained on a large time-series corpus; out-of-the-box zero-shot forecasting near per-dataset SOTA supervised models; handles varying history/prediction lengths and granularities. The frozen-backbone + train-readout pattern our B3 instrument already implements for our own body transfers directly: swap the body for a pretrained one, keep everything else (persistence rowing, Brier training, trust loop) unchanged.

entries.title: A decoder-only foundation model for time-series forecasting

entries.action: Selection/aggregation designs must measure joint errors, not member means: report pairwise simultaneous-error rate alongside skill. m5f trust-neutral + B1-drop consistent with members erring together on the same bars.
entries.note: ensemble effectiveness hinges on members NOT erring simultaneously; verification-aided selection targets joint-error structure. Our members are weakly correlated in output (mean|r| 0.26/0.35, CYCLE-216) yet m5f shows trust-vs-uniform neutral and m5g shows members jointly anti-informative — correlation of outputs under-describes failure; the object to measure is co-error on the same bars.
